name: Rock
about: Rock grew out of 1950s rock and roll, itself a collision of rhythm and blues, country and gospel in the American South, and by the mid-1960s it had become the dominant popular music of the West. Its core is electric guitar, bass and drums under a singer, built on backbeat and the twelve-bar form, but the family sprawls: the Beatles and Bob Dylan turned the LP into a statement, Led Zeppelin and Black Sabbath hardened it, punk stripped it back, and the alternative and indie generations of the 1980s and 1990s rebuilt it from the margins. Classic rock, psychedelia, progressive rock, punk, post-punk, hard rock and indie are the main branches. Its commercial centre has shifted to hip-hop and pop since the 2000s, but the form keeps renewing itself from the club level up.

artists.name: Chuck Berry
artists.why: rock and roll's first great songwriter

artists.name: The Beatles
artists.why: remade the album as a statement

artists.name: Bob Dylan
artists.why: brought literature to the electric band

artists.name: Neil Young
artists.why: ragged godfather of grunge and Americana

albums.title: Elvis Presley
albums.why: The first rock and roll LP to top the American charts, and the sound of Sun-era rawness arriving at RCA with the swagger intact.

albums.title: Chuck Berry Is on Top
albums.why: Effectively a singles collection, but it gathers the guitar licks and teenage narratives that every rock band since has borrowed from.

albums.title: Highway 61 Revisited
albums.why: Dylan plugged in and wrote a new language for rock in one summer; the band is loose, the words are furious and nothing has dated.

albums.title: Revolver
albums.why: Where the Beatles stopped being a beat group and turned the studio into an instrument, from the string octet to the tape loops.

albums.title: The Velvet Underground & Nico
albums.why: Barely sold at the time and spawned half of what followed: drone, noise, street-level lyrics and Lou Reed's deadpan all start here.

albums.title: Are You Experienced
albums.why: A debut that rewrote the electric guitar's vocabulary in forty minutes, uneven in places but overwhelming where it counts.

albums.title: After the Gold Rush
albums.why: Young's quietest great record, with the piano ballads and Crazy Horse stomps that set the template for a generation of ragged singer-songwriters.

albums.title: Led Zeppelin IV
albums.why: Zeppelin's most complete statement, balancing the folk and the hammer-of-the-gods sides and carrying the most famous song in rock radio history.

albums.title: Exile on Main St.
albums.why: A murky double album recorded in a French basement that turned out to be the Stones' deepest dive into blues, country and gospel.

albums.title: The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars
albums.why: Bowie's glam concept record is theatrical, tight and full of hooks; it made him a star and gave rock its first great alien.

albums.title: The Dark Side of the Moon
albums.why: The album-as-suite perfected, with Alan Parsons' engineering and Roger Waters' themes of time and madness holding it together end to end.

albums.title: Born to Run
albums.why: Springsteen's Phil Spector-sized bid for greatness, all highways and escape, the record that made the E Street Band a national institution.

albums.title: Marquee Moon
albums.why: Twin-guitar interplay from the CBGB scene with no punk sloppiness at all; the title track remains the standard for the long rock guitar piece.

albums.title: London Calling
albums.why: Punk's most generous record, opening out to reggae, rockabilly and soul while keeping the politics sharp and the choruses enormous.

albums.title: Remain in Light
albums.why: Byrne and Eno fused Afrobeat polyrhythms with art-school anxiety and made the 1980s' most forward-looking rock record.

albums.title: Murmur
albums.why: Mumbled, jangling and strangely beautiful, the record that gave American college rock its founding sound and its first great band.

albums.title: Doolittle
albums.why: Quiet-loud dynamics, surf guitar and surrealist screaming, in fifteen short songs that mapped the route to 1990s alternative rock.

albums.title: Nevermind
albums.why: The record that moved the underground to the centre of the culture, polished by Butch Vig without losing Cobain's hooks or his ache.

albums.title: OK Computer
albums.why: The last consensus rock masterpiece, where pre-millennial dread, guitar ambition and studio invention came together without a wasted minute.

albums.title: Is This It
albums.why: Eleven tight, deadpan songs that restarted guitar rock for a decade, with the Velvets' cool and a producer who kept everything dry.

albums.title: Yankee Hotel Foxtrot
albums.why: Jeff Tweedy's roots band frayed into static and ambient drift, and the result became the defining American rock record of its decade.

albums.title: Funeral
albums.why: Grief turned into communal anthems with accordions, strings and shouted choruses, the debut that made indie rock sound big again.

albums.title: Dogrel
albums.why: Dublin post-punk with a poet's ear and a pub band's drive, the strongest guitar-band debut of its decade from these islands.

albums.title: Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You
albums.why: A sprawling twenty-song double album where Adrianne Lenker's songwriting carries folk, country and noise rock with equal ease.
